<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix inflated draft-token counts for async `ngram_gpu` on Model Runner V1. Report worker-trimmed slots to the scheduler and exclude them from both aggregate and per-request acceptance statistics.

## Claims

- Count only valid ngram drafts, preserving statistics already accumulated for other requests when a request has no valid drafts.
- Keep aggregate and optional per-request draft counts consistent, including when grammar-invalidated drafts are also present.
- Correct statistics only: no change to proposal selection, sampling, or scheduled-token trimming; no throughput improvement is claimed.

## Validation

Local environment: Ubuntu 22.04 / WSL2, RTX 5090 Laptop GPU (24 GB), driver 610.62, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Triton 3.8.0. Model: cached `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` at revision `7ae557604adf67be50417f59c2c2f167def9a775`.

Base: `1a5b187066c918b2e23184560d703174dd542828`; initial fix: `14aceba778ea065beb608a416eaead0a4b4a3f6f`. Both used identical native artifacts from the base commit's official cu130 wheel. JSON records retain source SHA-256 hashes and the actual checkout; editable package version metadata alone does not identify the tested checkout.

Settings: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, FP16, greedy, seed 0, eager execution, prefix caching off, maximum output 128 tokens, model length 2048, maximum batched tokens 2048, maximum sequences 4. Ngram: `k=4`, lookup lengths 2–5. Twelve synthetic prompts per workload; a warm-up request was excluded from metric deltas. GPU runs explicitly enabled async scheduling; the CPU proposer reference disabled it (target inference still used the GPU).

| Initial run, ignore_eos=True | Submission batch size | Drafted | Accepted | Acceptance |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base, CPU ngram | 1 / 4 | 956 | 448 | 46.86% |
| Base, GPU ngram | 1 | 4336 | 448 | 10.33% |
| Base, GPU ngram | 4 | 4324 | 453 | 10.48% |
| Fixed, GPU ngram | 1 / 4 | 956 | 448 | 46.86% |

A second GPU run gave 4336/448 on the base and 956/448 on the fix at both batch sizes. The initial batched comparison had one output difference after EOS (generation deliberately continued past EOS); the same difference occurred between two base runs. The repeated base/fix pair matched 24/24 output token sequences. This does not establish general bitwise determinism.

With **normal EOS stopping**, base GPU ngram reported 2952 drafted / 236 accepted (7.99%), versus 622 / 236 (37.94%) after the fix, at both batch sizes. Output token sequences matched **24/24 requests**. A further run with the per-request follow-up enabled retained those counts and all 24 outputs; summed per-request drafted/accepted counts equaled the aggregate counters.

Repository tests:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_ngram_proposer_gpu.py -q
# 26 passed

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k 'spec_decoding_stats or per_request_spec_decode' -q
# 10 passed, 210 deselected
```

Seven added cases cover trimming counts by request ID, no/partial/all-invalid drafts, preserving another request's statistics, and combined grammar/ngram accounting. The four new scheduler cases produced 3 failures / 1 pass against the initially pushed fix, catching its missing per-request adjustment; all pass with the follow-up. Tests use the existing scheduler helper and real scheduler/output objects.

The follow-up is commit `3eea24abf3`. Full configured pre-commit checks passed in WSL, including Ruff, mypy and test-to-CI tethering. The additional GPU run used the same follow-up source before committing; its JSON records the dirty state and source hashes. The author personally reran the repository tests: 26 passed in 17.77s, followed by 10 passed / 210 deselected in 9.31s.

CI coverage: scheduler cases are included by the existing CPU `v1/core` job, and the V1 proposer test by the existing GPU `v1/spec_decode` job. Full project CI, CUDA graphs, V2 execution, larger models and throughput were not validated locally. This is a focused synthetic-model evaluation, not a general model-quality benchmark.

## Details

The V1 worker trims padded speculative slots before execution, while the scheduler retains its original padded draft count. Previously, the removed count never reached the scheduler, inflating the denominator. `update_scheduler_for_invalid_drafts()` now returns per-request removal counts, carried in optional `ModelRunnerOutput.ngram_invalid_spec_tokens`. The scheduler subtracts them alongside grammar-invalidated drafts. Empty/all-invalid requests preserve the aggregate accumulated for earlier requests. The follow-up applies the same deduction to optional per-request metrics.

This remains useful for deployments explicitly using MRV1. MRV2 uses a separate ngram implementation that fills unmatched slots with ordinary rejectable drafts; it does not use this V1 trimming/reporting path. This PR does not claim CPU/GPU acceptance parity for every model or for MRV2. The existing D2H completion wait is unchanged; the patch adds no GPU synchronization.

Related-work check on 2026-10-17: open-PR searches for `ngram acceptance`, `ngram_gpu invalid`, and `44056 in:body` found relevant overlap. [#52097](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52097) includes analogous accounting as part of its larger suffix_gpu feature and explicitly offers to rebase onto this existing PR. This PR keeps the fix scoped to existing ngram behavior. [#58356](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58356) optimizes the same trim loop without fixing the reporting path; its early return must preserve an empty dict if combined with this change. [#60339](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60339) targets MRV2 suffix decoding. These overlaps should be coordinated when merging.

Per-request acceptance metrics were added upstream in #48915 after this PR's original submission. The follow-up adapts the fix to that additional statistics path after rebasing.

AI assistance was used for the original implementation, rebase, regression tests, local validation, and this description. The human author reviewed the changes and personally ran the 36 passing repository tests above. The GPU experiments were executed with Codex assistance on the author's local machine.

Independent data point in case it helps review.

Setup: vLLM 0.31.0, Tesla T4, fp16, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, `num_speculative_tokens=4`, `prompt_lookup_min=2`, `prompt_lookup_max=5`, greedy, 30 single requests, `max_tokens=128`, counters read from `LLM.get_metrics()` (`vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts / _num_draft_tokens / _num_accepted_tokens`). I used vLLM's default scheduling settings and did not record whether async scheduling was active for the `ngram_gpu` runs.

| proposer | drafts | drafted tokens | accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ngram` (CPU) | 322 | 1,283 | 302 |
| `ngram_gpu` | 2,984 | 11,936 | 302 |

Accepted tokens agree, while drafted tokens are ~9.3x higher with `ngram_gpu`, so the reported acceptance rate is ~2.5% instead of ~23.5%. The CPU numbers equal an offline replay of `_find_longest_matched_ngram_and_propose_tokens` on vLLM's own outputs (30/30 requests), so the difference is in the `ngram_gpu` statistics, consistent with this PR's diagnosis. The same ~9-10x ratio appeared in all 9 `ngram_gpu` configurations I ran (greedy and sampling, batched, `max_num_seqs=4`, chunked long prompts, k=8).

Scripts and logs: https://github.com/novain-shibu/spectrace (`kaggle/matrix2/run.py`, `results/logs/spectrace-matrix-2.log`).

AI assistance (Claude) was used to run the experiments and draft this comment; I reviewed the numbers.

Updated this PR after rebasing and local validation. Commit 3eea24abf3 adds seven regression cases and applies the same invalid-ngram-draft deduction to the per-request metrics added upstream in #48915 after this PR's original submission.

The author reviewed the changes and personally reran the tests: 26 passed, then 10 passed (210 unrelated cases deselected). Full configured pre-commit checks passed locally in WSL. On Ubuntu 22.04 / WSL2 with an RTX 5090 Laptop GPU and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, the fixed async MRV1 GPU ngram counters matched the CPU proposer reference in the tested workload. Normal-EOS A/B outputs matched 24/24 requests, and a follow-up run confirmed per-request totals equal aggregate counts. The updated description includes the exact settings, limitations, and overlap with #52097 and #58356.

For the latest commit, hosted pre-commit was skipped after its contributor/label pre-run gate failed; Read the Docs then stopped because that same prerequisite failed. These are not results from running the code checks or compiling the documentation.

This is ready for maintainer review. AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and preparation of this update.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "ngram_invalid,grammar_invalid", [(0, 0), (2, 0), (3, 0), (1, 1)]
+)
+def test_ngram_invalid_drafts_excluded_from_stats(ngram_invalid, grammar_invalid):
+    """Trimmed slots must not inflate aggregate or per-request draft counts."""
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        async_scheduling=True,
+        num_speculative_tokens=3,
+        speculative_method="ngram_gpu",
+        use_v2_model_runner=False,
+        per_request_spec_decode_metrics="summary",
+    )
+    requests = create_requests(num_requests=2, num_tokens=1)
+    for request in requests:
+        scheduler.add_request(request)
+    prefill = scheduler.schedule()
+    scheduler.update_from_output(prefill, _make_model_runner_output(prefill))
+
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    first, second = (request.request_id for request in requests)
+    assert output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens == {
+        first: [-1] * 3,
+        second: [-1] * 3,
+    }
+    output.num_invalid_spec_tokens = {second: grammar_invalid}
+    runner_output = _make_model_runner_output(output)
+    runner_output.ngram_invalid_spec_tokens = {second: ngram_invalid}
+    valid = 3 - ngram_invalid - grammar_invalid
+    runner_output.sampled_token_ids = [[10, 11], [12, 13] if valid else [12]]
+    results = scheduler.update_from_output(output, runner_output)
+
+    stats = results[0].scheduler_stats.spec_decoding_stats
+    assert stats.num_drafts == 1 + bool(valid)
+    assert stats.num_draft_tokens == 3 + valid
+    assert stats.num_accepted_tokens == 1 + bool(valid)
+    assert stats.num_draft_tokens_per_pos == [1 + (i < valid) for i in range(3)]
+    for request, expected in zip(requests, [3, valid]):
+        metrics = request.spec_decode_metrics.to_dict()
+        assert metrics["num_draft_tokens"] == expected
+        assert metrics["num_accepted_draft_tokens"] == bool(expected)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("valid", [0, 2, 3])
+def test_trim_returns_invalid_counts_by_request(valid):
+    output = SchedulerOutput.make_empty()
+    output.scheduled_cached_reqs.req_ids = ["trimmed", "full", "missing", "no_draft"]
+    output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens = {

+    assert output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens == expected
+    assert output.num_scheduled_tokens == {
+        "trimmed": 1 + valid,
+        "full": 4,
+        "missing": 4,
+        "no_draft": 1,

Independent data point in case it helps review.

Setup: vLLM 0.31.0, Tesla T4, fp16, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, `num_speculative_tokens=4`, `prompt_lookup_min=2`, `prompt_lookup_max=5`, greedy, 30 single requests, `max_tokens=128`, counters read from `LLM.get_metrics()` (`vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts / _num_draft_tokens / _num_accepted_tokens`). I used vLLM's default scheduling settings and did not record whether async scheduling was active for the `ngram_gpu` runs.

| proposer | drafts | drafted tokens | accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ngram` (CPU) | 322 | 1,283 | 302 |
| `ngram_gpu` | 2,984 | 11,936 | 302 |

Accepted tokens agree, while drafted tokens are ~9.3x higher with `ngram_gpu`, so the reported acceptance rate is ~2.5% instead of ~23.5%. The CPU numbers equal an offline replay of `_find_longest_matched_ngram_and_propose_tokens` on vLLM's own outputs (30/30 requests), so the difference is in the `ngram_gpu` statistics, consistent with this PR's diagnosis. The same ~9-10x ratio appeared in all 9 `ngram_gpu` configurations I ran (greedy and sampling, batched, `max_num_seqs=4`, chunked long prompts, k=8).

Scripts and logs: https://github.com/novain-shibu/spectrace (`kaggle/matrix2/run.py`, `results/logs/spectrace-matrix-2.log`).
